guarantees.claim: When state_sel equals STATE_INIT, state_d is assigned state_init_i.
When state_sel equals STATE_ROUND, state_d is assigned add_round_key_out.
When state_sel equals STATE_CLEAR, state_d is assigned prd_clearing_state_i.
For any other state_sel value, state_d is assigned prd_clearing_state_i if key_len_i equals AES_256; otherwise state_d is assigned to itself (combinational latch).

assumptions.claim: The controlling FSM ensures state_sel stays within {STATE_INIT, STATE_ROUND, STATE_CLEAR} during normal operation.
assumptions.risk: If state_sel takes an unexpected value and key_len_i != AES_256, state_d latches its previous value, which could retain secret intermediate AES state and expose it to later read or side-channel analysis.

uncertain_points.claim: Default case latches state_d when key_len_i != AES_256, potentially retaining sensitive round or clearing state. The asymmetry between key lengths suggests either a missing clear or an intentional hold that may leak secrets.
uncertain_points.cond: state_sel is an undefined value and key_len_i != AES_256
uncertain_points.risk: If verified, latched state could be read later or leak via power/timing, violating secure wipe expectations.
